roadmap-facts-35b3b8f1e1.title: Ledger
roadmap-facts-35b3b8f1e1.source: - 2026-10-21: Memory audit. The default daemon had run 67 hours with 49 tabs that agents opened by name, one per task, and never closed: 17.4 GB across 47 WebKit processes and 90% of a CPU core, because a tab closed only with its daemon and a busy Mac never lets the daemon idle. Now a tab rests. After a third of `UMBRA_IDLE` unused it is hidden, so its timers slow and its animations pause as in a background tab; the next command shows it again and runs once the page reports itself visible. After all of `UMBRA_IDLE` it closes, and a command that names it says why. The back-forward cache is off: it kept every page a tab left frozen in memory (4 tabs after 6 pages each: 3.4 GB with it, 1.3 GB without). `bench/memory.py` keeps one agent working while others leave heavy tabs behind. With 10 one-page tabs left, memory once they are left went from 2756 to 331 MB and CPU from 15.3 to 1.9 seconds a minute. With 6 four-page tabs it went from 3863 to 312 MB, and the peak from 4271 to 1825 MB. Command latency is unchanged (bench.py, 20 runs). Results and charts: docs/evaluation/memory. The skill, MCP instructions, llms.txt and docs now tell agents to close their tabs. Measured, not adopted: one shared process pool (about 7 MB less per tab, through a deprecated API).

docs-evaluation-memory-readme-facts-a5e2.title: What we found
docs-evaluation-memory-readme-facts-a5e2.source: An audit of a real Mac on 2026-10-21 found the default profile's daemon running for 67 hours with 49 tabs open. Agents had opened every one of them by name for a task and never closed it. Together they held 17.4 GB across 47 WebKit processes and kept 90% of a CPU core busy. A tab closed only when its daemon exited, after 15 minutes without a command, and a Mac where agents work all day never gives it those 15 minutes. Every tab also kept running its animations and timers, because Umbra's pages always see themselves as visible.

docs-evaluation-memory-readme-facts-c1d3.title: What changed
docs-evaluation-memory-readme-facts-c1d3.source: - **A tab rests when no command uses it.** After a third of `UMBRA_IDLE` (5 minutes by default) Umbra hides it, so its timers slow and its animations pause, as a background tab does in Safari. The next command on it shows it again first. After all of `UMBRA_IDLE` (15 minutes) it closes, and its web process ends. [How it works](../../how-it-works.md#the-daemon).

docs-evaluation-memory-readme-facts-dd73.title: The measurement
docs-evaluation-memory-readme-facts-dd73.source: `bench/memory.py` starts a daemon under a throwaway profile. One agent opens a tab and takes a snapshot every 10 seconds for the whole run, which keeps the daemon busy as on a real Mac. Each of the other agents opens a heavy page in a tab of its own, takes a snapshot, clicks and reads the text, and never comes back. The heavy page holds memory the way a web app does: a JavaScript heap, a typed array, a drawn canvas, decoded images and a few thousand DOM nodes, kept busy by an animation and a timer. Every 5 seconds the bench adds up the physical footprint (Activity Monitor's Memory column) and CPU time of the daemon and of every process macOS holds it responsible for: its web content, GPU and networking processes. `UMBRA_IDLE` is 60 seconds here so a run takes minutes rather than an hour.

docs-evaluation-regression-results-facts.title: What the eval changed
docs-evaluation-regression-results-facts.source:
1. **The skill's safety rules were too blunt.** The first version said "get the user's explicit OK before purchases, posts, submissions, refunds…". The opus-skill refund candidate then stopped and asked for permission, even though the request said "Please refund it", and failed (13/14). The rules are now conditions on the request: do what was asked, ask before consequential actions that are your own idea, and use credentials the request provides. Re-run, the refund passed every time.
2. **`wait --idle` ignored `--timeout`.** An opus-bare candidate's `wait --idle` ran past two minutes and had to be killed. It's fixed in 2dd2701: it now fails at the timeout with a hint to wait for text or a selector.
3. **The harness itself had a bug.** One batch gave three reps of a task the same profile. The agents noticed tabs and sign-ins changing under them and moved to scratch profiles on their own, but the batch was discarded and re-run with a profile per run. The lesson went into the docs: parallel agents need separate profiles (or `--tab`), and cookies on 127.0.0.1 are shared across ports.

docs-evaluation-regression-results-facts.title: Reading the results
docs-evaluation-regression-results-facts.source: - Umbra is usable without the skill in the prompt: opus-bare passed everything with only `umbra help` in the task prompt, which suggests the CLI's help text holds up for agents (the installed skill was within their reach too, and their transcripts weren't kept to show whether they used it). The skill's value is efficiency and discipline: about 10× fewer help lookups, and none of opus-skill's runs fell back to `sleep`.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-4.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-4.source: The primary matrix is 1/4/8/16/32 concurrent workers, three repeats, with AB/BA arm order alternating by repetition. Each cell uses a fresh disposable profile, one persistent tab per worker and one persistent socket per worker. The matched route uses identical WebKit `read`/`fetch` commands. The public-http route changes only candidate static/JSON retrieval to its public no-cookie/no-JavaScript HTTP path. Report that routing difference and report both matrices; do not present it as an engine-only speedup. Baseline already uses its best browser `read`/`fetch` commands rather than navigation plus unnecessarily repeated extraction.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-c.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-c.source: Each cell records excluded warmups, every task and command latency, task success, matched socket and CLI control calls, physical-footprint samples, process membership and observed CPU. The sampler uses `bench/memory.py` responsibility-disclaimed launch and macOS responsibility attribution to include daemon plus responsible WebKit/GPU/network processes. Physical footprint is not RSS. Sample processing itself costs time, recorded as `samplerDurationMs`; the nominal sampling wait is 250 ms, and actual timestamp spacing includes sampler work. Fast process creation/exit between samples can escape peak and CPU observations. The fixture server and Python harness are excluded from browser-family memory/CPU. Raw timestamps make this limitation inspectable.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-0.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-0.source: A paired result is valid only when every task and warmup succeeds and both cells have active memory samples. Report distributions and repeat spread, not an isolated fastest cell. The 2× gate compares task throughput with both arms below the same explicit RAM budget (default 2 GiB); descriptive throughput/GiB ratios alone do not prove that gate. The 30% active footprint gate compares matched concurrency and workload using sampled whole-family peak. Sampling is too coarse to claim an exact instantaneous peak. Overall acceptance requires the complete matrix, no success regression and no per-task-type p95 regression above 10%, not any one passing row. A pair with any cell error or resource abort is ineligible even if its measured tasks happened to finish first. These are performance gates, not evidence of general agent reliability.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-2.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-2.source: The 24-hour release requirement was removed at the user’s explicit request on 2026-10-23. No 24-hour run is required for this delivery, and this release makes no 24-hour stability claim. `bench/soak.py` remains an optional diagnostic tool. The optional runner accepts at most 86400 seconds, validates the candidate hash on each cycle, performs all four task types plus repeated tab creation/closure, records actual PID/heartbeat/health/process samples, and cleans up on completion, interruption or failure. A short smoke run proves plumbing only. `final.json` must establish 24-hour duration, zero failures, successful cleanup and a post-warmup resource plateau before claiming long-run stability. No 24-hour soak was launched. A bounded smoke run can verify this optional tool’s plumbing; it does not establish long-duration stability.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-3.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-3.source: A whole-family hard safety guard applies to every primary arm and the soak. The default ceiling is 2048 MiB; budgets above 2048 MiB are rejected on this 16 GiB host. The first sample above budget terminates the test daemon, stops new command dispatch and preserves raw samples, abort reason and all planned tasks in the denominator. Sampling may overshoot by one interval; sampler failure itself also aborts. The 128 MiB deliberately low-ceiling baseline probe proves cleanup/abort plumbing; its peak is not a performance result. The soak samples the guard every second, streams guard samples to disk and retains one guard sample in memory. It never launches automatically.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-0.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-0.source: The separate `--admission` flag runs a secondary fixed-RAM experiment using the pre-candidate frozen `ADMISSION.json` (SHA256 `2214a4a68dd3ba7a4d2f5441bb693e8e85d7d149ad6faa1553d6147997a06378`). This does not change the primary matrix. Setup/tab creation, warmup, measured tasks and controls all pass through the same fresh-sampled admission controller in both arms. The controller uses a 1536 MiB watermark, 128 MiB in-flight reservations, a permanently reserved 128 MiB serial tab-keepalive worker, 180-second admission deadlines, and a 900-second cell deadline. All memory/CPU includes keepalive work; waits during measured tasks remain in their latency and throughput. Every admission and release forces a responsibility-family sample, so measurement overhead is intentionally included and reported. Setup failure cannot be repaired by reducing physical tab count. Ineligible cells stay in the matrix; passing a subset does not prove a full-matrix 2× target. The prepared command is:

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-9.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-9.source: Loaded controls and runtime semantic coverage are frozen separately in `CONTROL.json` (SHA256 `32aaaee29003ed718863467567aa91185fc794b9019abcf5abe20e242511de0c`). One independent persistent client runs `eval return 1` on existing worker-0 every 100 ms while measured workers execute. Missed cadence slots are skipped. Probe latency includes same-tab serialization and, in the secondary experiment, common admission waiting. In-flight probe completion remains in active wall time, CPU and footprint. Raw schedule/start/end timestamps and counts are retained. Loaded-control p95 has its own <=1.10 comparison gate; idle socket/CLI probes retain separate labels and cannot prove the loaded-control gate.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-f.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-f.source: The localhost fixture uses listen backlog 128 in every arm, above the maximum 32 worker grid. The configured backlog is retained in the campaign manifest.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-2.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-2.source: The multistep observation journey is frozen in `OBSERVATION.json` (SHA256 `d6c22cd7c57f16e6b9fd3da582597e494c21ba6fda39248388e022a066e4297f`). Its initial state, 12 action/read states and three navigation resets produce 16 observation states. Nine action states mutate input/output; three read bundles validate static HTML, JSON and JS DOM semantics. At every state the actual current Python SDK, CLI `--json`, and MCP tool transport independently produce forced-full and delta responses. Every delta reconstructs exact full snapshot text, ordered refs/count and document metadata; navigation must fall back to full. Every raw observation and generated step result is retained. Initial and reset full responses remain in the aggregate denominator. Each transport has separate actual tiktoken0.12.0/o200k_base canonical-result JSON byte/token totals and a50%gate. The SDK raw result retains its human `text`; actual CLI JSON omits `text` and retains `snapshot`; actual MCP content plus structured result is counted as delivered. These are observation-response counts under a fixed encoding, not end-to-end agent or GPT-6 billing-tokenizer claims. The original changed-point metric remains separate and cannot establish the multistep gate. Candidate campaigns require the actual `--sdk` source (default `sdk/python/umbra.py`), record its hash and verify it remained unchanged.

docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-4.title: Runtime workload protocol
docs-evaluation-runtime-protocol-facts-4.source: The verifier reads pending/history from `tasks` and scheduler/connection counters from `runtime`; those are distinct response shapes. The first retained campaign exposed this verifier mistake after its semantic actions, and a separate corrected 1/4/8/16/32 diagnostic verifies all bounds. Observation metadata reconstruction retains each transport’s requested-baseline state, inherits omitted keys only in delta mode, overlays emitted values, then requires all six metadata fields to match the independently forced-full result. Full/reset responses cannot inherit. Raw response payloads and token denominators are unchanged by these verifier corrections.

docs-how-it-works-facts-c3d09b5503.title: The daemon
docs-how-it-works-facts-c3d09b5503.source: The daemon exits after 15 minutes without a command (`UMBRA_IDLE` sets the limit in seconds). It never exits while a call is in flight, a handoff/sign-in window is open, or a tab has tracked unsaved input, an active download or a live lease. The `keepSignedIn` agent's visits don't count as commands here, so they never keep an idle daemon up. `umbra status` shows its process, profile, uptime and tabs, and `umbra stop` closes every tab and ends it.

docs-how-it-works-facts-be32a7d1dd.title: The daemon
docs-how-it-works-facts-be32a7d1dd.source: Tabs follow the same rule, one by one, so that the tabs agents leave behind don't pile up in a daemon that other agents keep busy. A tab no command has used for a third of the limit (5 minutes) rests: Umbra hides its window, and the page slows its timers and pauses its animations as a background tab does in Safari. The next command on it shows it again and runs once the page knows it is visible. A tab unused for the whole limit closes, and its web process ends with it; a later command that names it says so, and `open --tab NAME <url>` opens it again. A tab never rests while active or queued work targets it, a handoff shows it, a download is active, a lease protects it, or trusted form input marked it dirty, and a tab that closes while it was the current one leaves no current tab, so a command without `--tab` never lands in another agent's tab. On the way out it saves the session cookies of `keepSession` and `keepSignedIn` sites (see [sites.md](sites.md#keepsession)).

docs-how-it-works-facts-1028429c68.title: Tabs
docs-how-it-works-facts-1028429c68.source: Each tab is a `WKWebView` in a borderless, transparent, click-through window placed far off screen, at (-30000, -30000). WebKit's occlusion detection is turned off for these windows. As a result the page reports `document.visibilityState == "visible"`, runs `requestAnimationFrame` at about 30 frames a second, and fires `IntersectionObserver`. A web view that isn't in a window at all reports itself hidden and stalls its animation frames, which breaks lazy loading and infinite scroll. A tab left unused for 5 minutes is hidden on purpose, so it slows down as a background tab does, and shown again before the next command on it runs (see [the daemon](#the-daemon) above).

docs-how-it-works-facts-391e81018b.title: The cookie store
docs-how-it-works-facts-391e81018b.source: Session-only cookies (those without an expiry date) live in the daemon's memory, so they last as long as the daemon does. `keepSession` re-saves them with a 30-day expiry whenever a run or the daemon ends, which is what keeps single sign-on sessions alive between days. A site can still end a session on its side once it has gone unused for a while. For such a site `keepSignedIn` adds a launch agent that visits it every 10 minutes and then writes the cookies to disk (see [sites.md](sites.md#keepsignedin)).

docs-how-it-works-facts-315120c018.title: The one-shot commands
docs-how-it-works-facts-315120c018.source: `keep-signed-in` runs the same way: through the daemon when one is running, otherwise on its own. It never starts a daemon. For each site marked `keepSignedIn` it requests the probe path, or loads the root page, in a view that is never shown, keeps any cookies the answer sets, and then writes the store's cookies to disk. The `keepSignedIn` launch agent runs it every 10 minutes and logs to `keep-signed-in.log` in `~/Library/Application Support/Umbra/`.

docs-how-it-works-facts-3feef8ab12.title: The one-shot commands
docs-how-it-works-facts-3feef8ab12.source: Session commands have their own defaults, from a few seconds for an action to wait for its target up to 15 minutes for `handoff`. `umbra help <command>` shows them, and `--timeout` overrides any of them.

It checks without showing any page: a cookie site by its cookie in the store, a probe site by a request for its probe path in a view that is never shown, cancelled as soon as the status is known (a redirect counts as signed out), and a site with neither by its login page, loaded in such a view and watched until the site moves it on into itself or keeps it at a sign-in step ([sites.md](sites.md#signed-in-checks-cookie-or-probe)). Sign In asks the same way first, so a site you're signed in to never opens. It checks again each time the window is shown, and when the window comes to the front more than 30 seconds after the last check.

docs-runtime-readme-facts-f2d130d36a.title: See queued work and cancel it
docs-runtime-readme-facts-f2d130d36a.source: Explicit CLI/MCP budgets cover daemon connection retries and readiness; read/fetch/download share their original budget with store acquisition and one-shot fallback. After the execution deadline, CLI/MCP reply reads allow at most 100 ms to receive the daemon’s failure and cancellation details. This does not extend execution: a complete success received after the execution deadline is rejected, and an incomplete or later reply yields a local deadline error. Blocking request writes are unchanged, so this is a bound on connection/reply waiting rather than a hard whole-call wall-clock guarantee. Refused/full UNIX connections retry for at most one second within that budget; a missing socket keeps immediate cold startup.

docs-runtime-readme-facts-4de418f4ca.title: Extract records and wait for events
docs-runtime-readme-facts-4de418f4ca.source: `watch` uses DOM mutation and input/change/load events rather than repeated agent calls. It returns `matched: false` when its duration expires; durations are 0–25 seconds, with at most 16 watches per document. A programmatic value change that emits no observed event can be missed. Use ordinary `wait --js` when the condition needs polling or JavaScript computation. This is a one-result wait, not a durable event stream. General `wait --js` conditions react to DOM/input/load/visibility events too, retaining a 100 ms fallback for globals/time or unobserved changes. Predicates may run repeatedly; keep them free of side effects. Resources remain on demand and are removed on completion, cancellation, timeout or navigation.

docs-runtime-readme-facts-fe60cf83aa.title: Batch known steps and checkpoint a workflow
docs-runtime-readme-facts-fe60cf83aa.source: A batch runs 1–64 supported steps sequentially and stops at the first error. Each successful step returns a receipt. Failures retain indexed completed-step results and a failed-step record through CLI JSON errors, SDK errors and MCP structured content; exit codes and MCP error status remain failures. A failed step marked dispatched may already have changed the site. `before` and `after` use string conditions from `wait`: `js`, `url`, `text`, `selector` or `gone`. Steps name their target tab in `args` and use the parent’s agent/task and deadline. `batch` and `workflow` are coordinators, so they do not take a top-level CLI `--tab`. They are individual scheduler operations, not an atomic transaction across agents. Definitions are limited to 256 KiB and collected results to 4 MiB. Large outputs should go to files or use smaller observation budgets.

docs-runtime-readme-facts-c6d8b294a0.title: Inspect only when needed
docs-runtime-readme-facts-c6d8b294a0.source: The inspector is a token-protected IPv4-loopback dashboard for queue/ownership metadata, on-demand screenshots and human takeover. Its URL grants access to the profile inspector; keep it private. Optional live preview captures at one frame per second while enabled and visible; capture is off by default. `record` explicitly writes a PNG sequence and JSON manifest, bounded by duration (1–600 seconds), rate (0.1–5 fps), 600 frames and a 64 MiB maximum byte budget. Captures can contain signed-in page content. There is no video encoder or always-on recording service.

docs-security-facts-0e078b333c.title: Security model
docs-security-facts-0e078b333c.source: - **`keepSignedIn` runs in the background.** A launch agent sends each site you mark a request with your cookies every 10 minutes, so its session never idles out, and keeps the site's session-only cookies on disk as `keepSession` does. The agent is a per-user LaunchAgent: it runs as you, only while you're logged in, and needs no admin rights. Choosing **Keep Signed In** again in the site's **…** menu, or `umbra keep-signed-in <site> --off`, removes it once no site is marked. To remove it by hand, `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.randyren.umbra.keep-signed-in` and delete `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.randyren.umbra.keep-signed-in.plist` (a profile's label ends in `.<profile>`).

Mark `keepSession` on the ones whose sign-in rests on session cookies, such as university single sign-on, so the sign-in survives between runs. A site that still signs you out when you leave it alone for a while, as Canvas does, needs more: choose **Keep Signed In** from its **…** menu in the window, and Umbra visits it every 10 minutes so the session never goes idle (see [keepSignedIn](sites.md#keepsignedin)).

docs-sites-facts-88975382c7.title: Signed-in checks: cookie or probe
docs-sites-facts-88975382c7.source: - **`probeScript`:** Umbra fully loads `probe` (or `login`) so the app can refresh its tokens, then awaits the script once. The script can wait for app initialization and make a read-only authenticated request, returning a boolean. Tokens stay in the page; script exceptions, a non-boolean result or no answer within 30 seconds mean "couldn't check". A public app shell returning 200 or a stale cookie alone proves nothing. For example, `"probeScript": "return (await fetch('/api/me')).ok;"` checks a cookie-authenticated app. Bearer-token apps need their own authenticated request. Keep script code and site URLs trusted, and never return credentials.

docs-sites-facts-5dba2ba4ef.title: keepSignedIn
docs-sites-facts-5dba2ba4ef.source: With `"keepSignedIn": true`, Umbra visits the site every 10 minutes, so the session is never idle long enough to end. It implies `keepSession`: the site's session-only cookies are kept for 30 days whether or not `keepSession` is set.

docs-sites-facts-9fc49fa2ca.title: keepSignedIn
docs-sites-facts-9fc49fa2ca.source: **Open tabs look attended:** some sites also sign you out from inside an open page that gets no keystroke, mouse move or scroll for a while. Air Canada does it after 15 minutes, "stay signed in" or not. An agent's tab never gets that kind of input, so a tab left on such a site would sign you out everywhere. While the daemon runs, any of its tabs on a `keepSignedIn` site gets a Shift key tap every 15 seconds, which the page counts as input and which changes nothing on it. Tabs a command is using, and handoff windows, are left alone.

docs-sites-facts-05542aa6d4.title: keepSignedIn
docs-sites-facts-05542aa6d4.source: **The launch agent:** the visits come from a launchd job in your login session (a LaunchAgent). It runs `umbra keep-signed-in` once when it's installed, at each login, and every 10 minutes by the clock (on the hour, ten past, and so on).

docs-sites-facts-774428b88e.title: keepSignedIn
docs-sites-facts-774428b88e.source: **The trade-off:** every 10 minutes Umbra sends the site a request with your cookies, for as long as the agent runs, and the site sees a session that is never idle. The cookies sit on disk as they do with `keepSession`. Turn it on only for the sites that sign you out too soon, and only on a Mac you trust.

docs-sites-facts-63bc9e1ed5.title: Using sites from the command line
docs-sites-facts-63bc9e1ed5.source: Named sites that are already signed in return at once (exit 0) and open nothing. Otherwise the window opens each login page in turn and the command returns once all are signed in; it exits 3 if the window is closed first and 2 after `--timeout` (default 900 seconds). The profile's daemon shows the window, so other commands keep working meanwhile. An unknown name exits 64 and lists the names it knows. With no sites file and no arguments, `umbra sign-in` exits 64 and explains how to name a URL instead.

sdk-readme-facts-cff605c48a.title: Deadlines, cancellation and errors
sdk-readme-facts-cff605c48a.source: Python and TypeScript deadlines are absolute Unix timestamps in **seconds**, not milliseconds; Swift accepts an absolute `Date`. They cover the client queue, connection and reply. The SDK forwards the same deadline as `args.deadline` so the runtime can expire work too. Defaults are 30 seconds per call. Closing a client closes its socket; it never sends `stop` or deletes the profile.

sdk-readme-facts-bbe364fd3e.title: Deadlines, cancellation and errors
sdk-readme-facts-bbe364fd3e.source: Replies default to a **16 MiB bound**, including the JSON-line framing. Configure `max_reply_bytes` (Python) / `maxReplyBytes` (TypeScript and Swift) for larger screenshots or downloads. Oversized or malformed replies close the socket; a later explicit command can establish another connection. This is reconnection, not replay of the failed command.
